items.title: Apache JSPWiki: Session fixation in the login flow
items.summary: Session Fixation in the login flow of Apache JSPWiki versions 2.10 through 3.0.0 on all platforms. The session identifier was not replaced when a user authenticated, so an attacker who could set a known session identifier in the browser of a victim could use the same identifier after the victim logged in. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1 (3.x) or 2.12.6 (2.x), which fix this issue.

items.title: Apache JSPWIKI: Page level ACL bypass
items.summary: Wiki page level access control list bypass in Apache JSPWIKI versions prior to 3.0.1 on all platforms allows an attacker to bypass page level access controls through a specifically crafted wiki page. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1 which fixes this issue.

items.title: Apache JSPWIKI: CsrfProtectionFilter improperly implemented on specific pages
items.summary: Cross Site Request Forgery in multiple components in Apache JSPWIKI on the specified versions on all platforms allows an attacker to bypass CSRF protections under specific conditions and http methods. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

items.title: Apache JSPWiki: Unsafe reflection causes Denial of Service
items.summary: Denial of Service in DefaultPluginManager in Apache JSPWIKI versions prior to the fixed version on all platforms allows an attacker to spawn multiple threads until resource exhaustion or to class load any class on the classpath and creating an instance of it. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

items.title: WordPress Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor plugin <= 5.1.4 - Broken Access Control vulnerability
items.summary: Missing Authorization vulnerability in BdThemes Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor bdthemes-prime-slider-lite allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Prime Slider – Addons For Elementor: from n/a through 5.1.4.

items.title: Apache JSPWiki: XSS in ListLocksPlugin
items.summary: Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in ListLocksPlugin in Apache JSPWiki 2.10.2 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows an attacker to execute javascript in the browser of a visitor of a page that uses the plugin. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

When this variable isn't set, the cli, phpdbg and embed SAPIs default to the CLI mode, and errors are rendered with CliErrorRenderer. items.title: Doctrine Remember-Me Token Provider Accepts Outdated Tokens Under the Series of Their Copy, Also After Logout
items.summary: DoctrineTokenProvider keeps a copy of the previous token of a remember-me cookie. This way, concurrent requests sent with that token are still accepted for 60 seconds. The copy is stored in another row, under a series derived from the series of the cookie. Since Symfony 6.4.45, 7.4.18 and 8.1.6, a copy is stored for every series that the remember-me handler generates. Before, copies were stored only for the series…

items.title: Mailer's require tls Can Be Bypassed by a Man in the Middle
items.summary: Since Symfony 7.3, the require tls option of EsmtpTransport refuses to send a message over a connection that isn't encrypted. It prevents a network attacker from stripping STARTTLS. But when the server rejected the EHLO command, the transport fell back to HELO and skipped that check. An attacker in the middle of an SMTP connection that uses STARTTLS could answer EHLO with an error and HELO with a success. The…

items.title: Trailing-Slash and Scheme Redirects Send Paths Starting With // to Another Host
items.summary: The router redirects a request to the same URL with or without its trailing slash, or with the scheme that a route requires. To do so, the matcher returns RedirectController::urlRedirectAction() with the path info of the request as path. Since Symfony 5.4.44, 6.4.12 and 7.1.5, urlRedirectAction() turns a path that starts with // into ://..., so that protocol-relative targets configured in routes work. The path info…

items.title: Apache JSPWIKI: CsrfProtectionFilter not applied in 3.0.0
items.summary: Cross Site Request Forgery protections are improperly configured in jspwiki.war in Apache JSPWIKI 3.0.0 on all platforms allows attacker to bypass protections for CSRF. A work around exists for existing deployments. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1 which fixes this issue.

items.title: Apache JSPWIKI: Token exposure
items.summary: Token Exposure in AttachmentTab.jsp in Apache JSPWIKI in the effected version on all platforms exposes the Cross Site Request Forgery protected token via the address bar. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1 which fixes this issue.

items.title: soapbar: verify envelope bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)

There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify envelope bsp()…

items.title: github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp permits denial of service through a malformed IPv4 payload length
items.summary: In github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp/dhcpv4/nclient4, BroadcastRawUDPConn.ReadFrom does not validate that the IPv4 payload length is sufficient to hold a UDP header before calculating the DHCP payload length. A frame with an IPv4 total-length field specifying fewer than eight payload bytes results in a negative DHCP length, causing a panic in buf.Consume due to a negative slice bound.

items.title: Cakephp twig-view unserialize Twig filter allows arbitrary object deserialization
items.summary: Impact The unserialize filter has no restriction on which classes are allowed. This can be used as a deserialization remote-code-execution gadget. Patches 1.3.3 and 2.1.2 contain a fix for this issue. The fix may impact backwards compatibility if you are relying on deserializing PHP objects in your templates. Workarounds Don't use the unserialize filter.

items.summary: Drupal Core contains a not failing securely vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take over an existing site or execute arbitrary code via the Drupal installer. Under specific conditions, the attacker can use install.php to attempt to reinstall Drupal on the site.

The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

items.title: Optimizely Web Experimentation External Control of Critical State Data Vulnerability

Successful exploitation can result in attacker-controlled JavaScript being distributed through Optimizely-hosted assets and executed in browsers visiting affected customer websites.
